Best AI Audio Tools

Explore AI tools for voiceover, podcast cleanup, music ideation, and faster audio production workflows.

By LokkeeVerse Editorial · 16 min read

Best AI Audio Tools in 2026: Voice Generation, Music and Audio Editing

AI audio tools are changing how creators, musicians, podcasters, businesses and video producers create and edit sound. Tasks that once required a recording studio, professional voice actor or expensive audio software can now be completed with AI-powered platforms.

Whether you need realistic voiceovers for YouTube videos, original background music for social media, cleaner podcast recordings or AI-generated songs, there are tools designed for different stages of audio production.

The challenge is choosing the right platform. Some tools specialize in natural-sounding speech, while others focus on music generation, podcast editing, noise removal or audio transcription. Understanding these differences can help you save time and avoid paying for features you do not need.

This guide explores the best AI audio tools in 2026, their main capabilities, who they are best suited for and how to choose the right option for your workflow.

What Are AI Audio Tools?

AI audio tools are software applications that use artificial intelligence to generate, analyze, improve or edit sound. They can convert written text into speech, create songs from prompts, remove background noise, transcribe conversations and help users edit recordings more efficiently.

Common uses include:

  • Creating voiceovers for YouTube videos, advertisements and online courses.
  • Generating original songs and background music.
  • Producing and editing podcasts.
  • Cleaning up noisy recordings and improving speech clarity.
  • Translating or dubbing audio into other languages.
  • Transcribing interviews, meetings and voice notes.
  • Creating sound effects for games, animations and videos.
  • Developing conversational voice assistants and automated customer support systems.

The best tool depends on the final result you want. A music generator is not necessarily the right choice for professional narration, and a voice generator will not replace a full audio editing application.

Best AI Audio Tools at a Glance

  • ElevenLabs: Best for realistic AI voices and text-to-speech.
  • Suno: Best for generating complete songs with vocals.
  • Udio: Best for exploring musical styles and creating song variations.
  • Descript: Best for editing podcasts and spoken recordings using text.
  • Adobe Podcast: Best for improving the clarity of voice recordings.
  • Murf AI: Best for business presentations and professional voiceovers.
  • Speechify: Best for listening to written content.
  • Auphonic: Best for automated audio leveling and post-production.
  • Krisp: Best for reducing background noise during calls.
  • Riverside: Best for recording remote interviews and podcasts.

These recommendations reflect the tools' primary use cases rather than a universal ranking. The best option for a musician may be very different from the best choice for a YouTube creator or business.

1. ElevenLabs: Best for Realistic AI Voices

ElevenLabs is an AI audio platform known for generating natural-sounding speech from written text. It is useful for creators who need narration without recording every line themselves.

Users can create voiceovers for videos, audiobooks, advertisements, educational content and other spoken projects. Depending on the available model and plan, the platform also supports features such as voice cloning, multilingual speech, dubbing and speech-to-text workflows.

Key Features

  • Text-to-speech generation with expressive delivery.
  • A selection of synthetic voices and voice customization options.
  • Voice cloning features subject to eligibility and consent requirements.
  • Multilingual speech generation and dubbing capabilities.
  • Audio generation tools for different creative workflows.
  • Developer APIs for integrating speech into applications.

Who Should Use ElevenLabs?

ElevenLabs is a strong option for YouTubers, audiobook creators, developers, educators and businesses that need realistic narration. It can be particularly useful for faceless video channels that rely on voiceovers.

However, generated speech should be reviewed for pronunciation, pacing and emotional consistency. Voice cloning should only be used with appropriate permission, and users should check the platform's current licensing conditions before using generated audio commercially.

2. Suno: Best for AI-Generated Songs

Suno is designed to generate music from written descriptions. Users can describe a genre, mood, theme or musical arrangement and create a song without needing to perform every instrument or record vocals manually.

It is useful for experimenting with musical ideas, producing demos and creating songs for personal projects. Depending on the current features available, users can also provide lyrics, explore different styles and develop variations of generated tracks.

Key Features

  • Song generation from text prompts.
  • AI-generated vocals and instrumental arrangements.
  • Support for a wide range of musical styles.
  • Tools for exploring variations and developing musical ideas.
  • Creative workflows for people without formal music-production experience.

Who Should Use Suno?

Suno is suitable for aspiring musicians, content creators, independent artists and people experimenting with songwriting. It can help users move from an idea to a musical draft quickly.

Before using a generated track in a monetized YouTube video, advertisement or client project, review the current terms for the specific plan. Commercial-use permissions, platform rules and copyright considerations can affect how the music may be distributed.

3. Udio: Best for Exploring Musical Styles

Udio is another AI music-generation platform that helps users turn musical descriptions into songs. It is useful for exploring different genres, arrangements and creative directions without building every track from scratch.

Rather than treating the first output as a finished product, creators can use music-generation tools to compare alternatives, refine their ideas and develop a sound that fits their project.

Key Features

  • Music generation from text descriptions.
  • Experimentation with different genres and moods.
  • Song variations and creative development workflows.
  • Opportunities to explore instrumental and vocal arrangements.
  • Support for rapid music ideation.

Who Should Use Udio?

Udio may suit musicians, video creators and producers who want to explore different musical directions. It can also help beginners understand how changes in mood, instrumentation and genre influence a generated track.

Compare its results with other music generators using the same prompt. Listen for arrangement quality, vocal clarity and consistency rather than judging a tool by a single impressive sample.

4. Descript: Best for Podcast and Spoken-Audio Editing

Descript combines transcription with audio and video editing. One of its most useful features is the ability to edit spoken recordings through their transcripts.

For example, a podcaster can identify an unwanted sentence in a transcript and remove the corresponding audio. This approach can make editing interviews, tutorials and presentations more accessible to people who are not familiar with traditional audio-editing software.

Key Features

  • Automatic transcription of recorded speech.
  • Text-based editing for supported audio and video workflows.
  • Tools for reducing filler words and tightening recordings.
  • Voice and sound enhancement features, depending on the plan.
  • Collaboration and production tools for content teams.

Who Should Use Descript?

Descript is useful for podcasters, interviewers, educators, marketers and YouTubers who regularly work with spoken content.

It is especially valuable when the main task is removing mistakes, reorganizing dialogue or preparing a recording for publication. Always listen to the final version because automated edits can remove important pauses or make natural conversation sound unnatural.

5. Adobe Podcast: Best for Cleaning Up Voice Recordings

Adobe Podcast provides browser-based tools designed to improve spoken audio. Its speech-enhancement capabilities can help make recordings sound clearer when the original audio contains background noise or room-related imperfections.

This is useful when recording equipment is limited or a speaker has recorded content in a less-than-ideal environment.

Key Features

  • AI-powered speech enhancement.
  • Tools for improving voice clarity.
  • Recording and production features for supported workflows.
  • Browser-based access to relevant audio-processing features.

Who Should Use Adobe Podcast?

Adobe Podcast is a useful option for creators recording voiceovers at home, students preparing presentations, podcasters and businesses producing spoken content.

It cannot make every poor recording sound perfect. Distorted audio, very low recording levels and severe clipping may remain noticeable after enhancement. For better results, record close to the microphone in a quiet space and use AI enhancement as a finishing step.

6. Murf AI: Best for Professional Business Voiceovers

Murf AI focuses on AI voice generation for business and educational content. It helps users produce narration for presentations, training materials, explainers and marketing videos.

Its workflow is designed around turning scripts into voiceovers, with options for selecting voices and adjusting delivery where supported.

Key Features

  • Text-to-speech voice generation.
  • Voice selection and narration customization.
  • Tools for creating business presentations and training content.
  • Workflows for educational and promotional videos.
  • Features that support structured voiceover production.

Who Should Use Murf AI?

Murf AI is suitable for corporate trainers, marketing teams, instructional designers and businesses that regularly produce narrated content.

It may be a better fit than a music-focused platform when the primary requirement is consistent, professional narration. Before subscribing, test the voices with your actual script, including names, technical terms and words commonly used by your audience.

7. Speechify: Best for Listening to Written Content

Speechify converts written material into spoken audio. It is useful for people who prefer listening to articles, documents and other text instead of reading everything on a screen.

Depending on the product and plan, it can support text-to-speech workflows involving documents, webpages and other written materials.

Key Features

  • Text-to-speech conversion.
  • Voice and playback-speed options.
  • Support for listening to written content across supported devices.
  • Features for accessibility and reading productivity.

Who Should Use Speechify?

Speechify can benefit students, professionals, researchers and people who want to listen to lengthy documents while completing other tasks.

It is primarily a listening and reading tool rather than a complete music-production suite. If you need to create original songs or edit complex podcast sessions, a specialist audio platform will be more appropriate.

8. Auphonic: Best for Automated Audio Post-Production

Auphonic helps users prepare audio for publication through automated processing. It is particularly relevant to podcasts, interviews, spoken-word recordings and other projects where consistent sound levels matter.

Rather than generating a complete song or synthetic voice, it focuses on improving and standardizing existing recordings.

Key Features

  • Loudness normalization.
  • Automatic level adjustment.
  • Noise and hum reduction features, depending on the processing options.
  • Audio post-production workflows.
  • Tools for preparing recordings for distribution.

Who Should Use Auphonic?

Auphonic is useful for podcasters, journalists, educators and production teams who need a consistent listening experience across episodes.

It can help reduce the amount of manual adjustment needed when speakers record at different volumes. However, it should be used alongside good recording practices, not as a replacement for checking the final mix.

9. Krisp: Best for Noise Cancellation During Calls

Krisp is designed to reduce unwanted background noise in real-time communication. It can help make speech clearer during online meetings, remote interviews and calls.

Unlike music generators, it focuses on the audio people hear during communication rather than creating new musical content.

Key Features

  • AI-powered background-noise suppression.
  • Support for clearer voice communication.
  • Tools designed for online meetings and calls.
  • Compatibility with supported communication applications and devices.

Who Should Use Krisp?

Krisp is worth considering for remote workers, customer support agents, freelancers, online tutors and people who regularly participate in virtual meetings.

Its usefulness depends on the quality of the original microphone signal and the type of background noise. Test it with your microphone and preferred meeting application before relying on it for important calls.

10. Riverside: Best for Remote Podcast Recording

Riverside is a recording and production platform designed for podcasts, interviews and other remote conversations. Its workflows can help creators record participants in different locations and prepare the resulting content for publication.

Its exact AI features depend on the current product and subscription plan.

Key Features

  • Remote audio and video recording.
  • Separate participant recordings in supported workflows.
  • Podcast production tools.
  • Transcription and content-repurposing features where available.
  • Tools for organizing and preparing recorded conversations.

Who Should Use Riverside?

Riverside is useful for podcast hosts, interviewers, businesses and creators who record conversations with remote guests.

It is particularly relevant when recording quality matters and participants cannot meet in person. For the best results, ask guests to use headphones, record in a quiet environment and test their microphones before starting.

How to Choose the Best AI Audio Tool for Your Needs

Choosing the right tool becomes easier when you start with the task you want to complete.

If You Need AI Voiceovers

Consider ElevenLabs or Murf AI. Both focus on turning written scripts into spoken audio, although their interfaces, voice options and production workflows differ.

Test the same paragraph in each platform. Pay attention to pronunciation, natural pauses, emotional delivery and how well the voice fits your audience.

If You Want to Create Original Music

Start with Suno or Udio. Describe the mood, genre, tempo and instrumentation you want, then compare the generated tracks.

For example, a video creator might request calm ambient music for a tutorial, while a filmmaker might need dramatic instrumental music for a suspenseful scene. Specific prompts usually make it easier to evaluate the results.

If You Need to Edit a Podcast

Consider Descript for transcript-based editing, Riverside for remote recording and production, or Auphonic for automated audio processing.

These tools solve different problems, so the best choice depends on whether you need to record guests, edit dialogue or standardize the final sound.

If Your Recording Has Background Noise

Adobe Podcast and Krisp are worth evaluating. Adobe Podcast is suited to improving recorded speech, while Krisp is focused on real-time communication.

Choose based on whether you need to clean an existing file or improve the audio people hear during a live call.

If You Want to Listen to Documents

Speechify is designed for turning written material into speech. It can be useful for listening to articles, notes and other documents while working or studying.

Are AI Audio Tools Free?

Some AI audio platforms offer free plans, limited trials or a restricted number of generations. These options are useful for testing quality before committing to a subscription.

However, free access does not always include every feature or permission.

Before choosing a tool, check:

  • Monthly generation or transcription limits.
  • Whether exported audio includes a watermark or other restriction.
  • Available voice and language options.
  • File length and export-quality limitations.
  • Whether voice cloning or advanced editing requires a paid plan.
  • Whether the plan permits commercial use.
  • Whether unused credits expire.

Subscription prices and plan limits can change, so check the official pricing page for the specific tool before paying. If you are starting with a small budget, test a free tier first and upgrade only when you encounter a limitation that affects your work.

Can You Use AI-Generated Audio for YouTube Monetization?

AI-generated audio can be part of a monetized YouTube video, but using an AI tool does not automatically make a video eligible for monetization.

The finished content must comply with YouTube's monetization policies and applicable copyright rules. Videos that offer meaningful original commentary, storytelling, education or creative value are generally a stronger foundation than channels that publish repetitive, mass-produced material with little original contribution.

For example, a creator could use an AI voice to narrate an original news explainer, add licensed background music and edit the video with original commentary and visuals. The creator still needs to verify the rights for every audio asset and follow applicable disclosure requirements.

Before publishing, confirm that:

  • Your plan allows the intended commercial use.
  • You have the necessary rights to the music, voice or recording.
  • You have permission to clone a real person's voice.
  • Your use of third-party material complies with applicable copyright rules.
  • Your video satisfies the platform's current monetization policies.
  • Any required disclosure of realistic synthetic or altered content is provided.

AI audio is a production aid, not a guarantee of copyright clearance or monetization approval.

Important Safety and Copyright Considerations

AI audio tools make it easier to imitate voices and generate music, but this creates responsibilities for users.

Voice cloning should be performed only with appropriate authorization. Do not use a person's synthetic voice to mislead an audience, impersonate someone or suggest that they endorsed a product when they did not.

Music rights also require careful attention. A platform's terms may distinguish between personal use, commercial use, distribution and content created under different subscription plans. Permission to use a generated track does not necessarily settle every copyright question involving the output.

For commercial projects, retain relevant licence information, review the terms in effect when you create the asset and keep records of any permissions you obtain.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best AI audio tool overall?

ElevenLabs is a strong starting point for realistic AI speech, Suno is suitable for generating complete songs, and Descript is useful for editing spoken recordings. The best overall choice depends on the kind of audio you need to produce.

Which AI tool can generate a song from text?

Suno and Udio are two options for generating music from text prompts. Results vary depending on the prompt, genre, desired arrangement and platform capabilities.

Which AI audio tool is best for YouTube creators?

ElevenLabs can help with narration, Suno can generate music ideas, Descript can edit spoken content, and Adobe Podcast can improve voice recordings. A creator may use more than one tool to complete a video.

Can AI audio tools clone my voice?

Some platforms provide voice-cloning features, subject to their requirements and restrictions. You should use your own voice or another voice only when you have the appropriate authorization.

Do I need professional equipment to use AI audio tools?

No. Many tools work through a browser or desktop application and do not require a professional studio. A reasonably good microphone, a quiet recording environment and headphones can still improve the final result significantly.

Can AI-generated music be used commercially?

Some platforms permit commercial use under particular plans or conditions. You must check the current terms for the exact tool and subscription you use. Do not assume that every track generated on a free plan is cleared for commercial use.

Can AI audio tools remove all background noise?

No. Noise reduction can improve many recordings, but severe distortion, clipping, echo and overlapping voices can be difficult to repair completely. Recording clean audio from the beginning remains important.

Final Verdict

The best AI audio tools in 2026 are specialized platforms that help users generate speech, create music, improve recordings and edit audio more efficiently.

For realistic voiceovers, start with ElevenLabs. For AI-generated songs, explore Suno or Udio. For transcript-based podcast editing, consider Descript. Adobe Podcast is worth testing for recorded speech enhancement, while Auphonic can help standardize audio levels and Krisp can improve communication in noisy environments.

You do not need to subscribe to every platform. Start with the one that solves your biggest problem, test it using a real project and review its quality, limitations and licensing terms. As your production needs grow, you can combine complementary tools into a workflow that saves time without sacrificing originality or sound quality.
